name: SALTO
aliases: Laparoscopic versus open sacrocolpopexy for vault prolapse
registry: Dutch Trial Register NTR3276; long-term follow-up NTR6330
question: Does laparoscopic sacrocolpopexy improve prolapse-related quality of life compared with open abdominal sacrocolpopexy for post-hysterectomy vault prolapse?

design.population: Seventy-four women with symptomatic post-hysterectomy vaginal vault prolapse choosing surgery, with or without cystocele or rectocele, were randomized in four teaching and two university hospitals in the Netherlands.
design.locator: Primary full text, Materials and methods; Results, Figure 1

verdictNote: UDI prolapse-domain superiority was not shown; blood loss and hospital stay favored laparoscopy.
takeaway: Laparoscopic versus open abdominal sacrocolpopexy for post-hysterectomy vault prolapse did not improve the prespecified 12-month UDI prolapse-domain score; laparoscopy reduced blood loss and hospital stay in secondary analyses.

delivery.label: Operative technique
delivery.value: Experienced gynecologists (at least 50 prior procedures) used two strips of type 1 polypropylene mesh, each 3 cm wide and approximately 15 cm long, secured to anterior and posterior vaginal walls with nonabsorbable multifilament sutures and to the sacral promontory with staples or sutures in the open arm and staples in the laparoscopic arm; mesh was reperitonealized. Laparoscopy used four ports; open surgery preferably used a Pfannenstiel incision.
